3. MVC Nos.791/2016 and 792/2016 were arising out of common accident and therefore, the MACT took up both the matters together for trial and passed common judgment.

Claimants in MVC No.791/2016 have filed MFA No.103245/2017 claiming for enhancement of compensation and insurer of the vehicle (TATA 407) has filed MFA No.104100/2017 against the said judgment contending that he was not liable to pay the compensation since there was violation of permit condition.

Similarly claimants in MVC 792/2016 have filed MFA No.102595/2017 praying for enhancement of compensation and the insurer of the vehicle filed MFA No.104101/2017 contending that it was not liable to pay the compensation since there was violation of permit condition.
All these four appeals arise out of common judgment and award passed in MVC No.791/2016 and 792/2016.

4. For sake of convenience, we refer the parties as their rank before the Tribunal.

5. It was the case of the claimants in both the case that on 21.02.2016, deceased Ramachandra @
Ramesh Laxman Donkari and deceased Vinod Annappa Parit were going in the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA.22/EM 4450.
Deceased Ramachandra @ Ramesh was riding the said vehicle and deceased Vinod was pillion rider.
They were proceeding on Belagavi-Sankeshwar road.

They met with an accident at Muktimath of Bennalli village due to rash and negligent driving of LGV TATA 407 vehicle bearing KL.05/M.1754 (hereinafter referred as TATA 407) driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of impact, both the rider of motorcycle sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the spot.
Criminal case was registered against the driver of the said TATA 407 vehicle and he was charge sheeted by the police.
6. It was contention of claimants in MVC 791/2016 that the deceased Ramachandra was aged 30 years at the time of the accident.
He had a transport business and from the said business, he used to earn Rs.10,000/- per month.
He had a kirana shop and from the same, he used to earn - 10 - C/W MFA Nos.104100/2017, 102695/2017 and 104101/2017.
Rs.20,000/- per month.
He had also agricultural lands and used to earn Rs.2,00,000/- per annum from agriculture.
From the said income, he used to maintain the family.
Petitioners, being wife and minor daughter of deceased, were depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
With these reasons claimants in MVC 791/2016 had filed petition to award Rs.80,00,000/- as compensation.
7. It was contention of petitioners in MVC No.792/2016 that deceased was aged about 33 years at the time of the accident.
He was running a laundry and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
He had agricultural lands and was earning Rs.2,00,000/- per annum from the agriculture.
Claimants being widow and minor children of Vinod have claimed to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.

8. In MVC 791/2016, the claimants had impleaded owner and insurer of TATA 407 vehicle and in MVC 792/2016 claimants have impleaded owner as well as insurer of TATA 407 of vehicle so also legal heirs of owner and insurer of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA.22/EM. 4450.
The deceased Ramachandra was the owner of the - 11 - C/W MFA Nos.104100/2017, 102695/2017 and 104101/2017.
said motor vehicle.
Owner of TATA 407 vehicle did not appear before the Tribunal.

8 9. Insurer of the said vehicle in both the cases had filed written statement and contentions of the respondent in both the cases are, more or less similar.

The insurer had contended that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider and denied that it was caused due to negligence of the driver of the said TATA 407.
It had further contended that respondent No.1 was the owner of the said vehicle from 8.5.2015 till 7.5.2016 and he had sold the said vehicle.
He sold the said vehicle to one Kunju Baba Abdul Khadar of Chikodi without intimation to insurer and the vehicle records were transferred in the name of said Kunju Baba.
It was in the name of said Kunju Baba for the period from 20.01.2016 till 04.02.2017.
Thereafter, the said Kunju Baba sold the vehicle in favour of S.F. Peerjade of Chikodi without transferring the insurance certificate and also without intimation to the insurer.
The policy of insurance was also not transferred in the name of the present purchaser.

Therefore, the insurer is not liable to - 12 -  C/W MFA Nos.104100/2017,
 102695/2017 and 104101/2017.
pay the compensation.

Respondent No.3 has further contend that, as on the date of the accident, policy of insurance was not in force and even if it was in force, the owner of the vehicle had violated the terms and condition of policy of insurance and driver of the vehicle had no valid and effective licence.
Therefore, respondent-insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
With these reasons prayed for dismissal of the petitions.
10. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal has framed relevant issues.
11. Claimants in MVC Nos.791/2016 and 792/2016 examined PW-1 and PW.2 and they got marked Ex.P1 to P11.

The respondent/insurer did not lead oral evidence but got marked policy of insurance as Ex.R1 and R2.
12.
The Tribunal, on appreciating the pleading and evidence on record, partly allowed both the petitions.

It had awarded compensation of Rs.10,21,000/- to the claimants in both the petitions with interest at the rate of 6% per annum by impugned judgment and award dated 03.06.2017.

We have heard the arguments of the learned advocate for the claimants so also the learned advocate for the insurer of TATA 407.
15.

The following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought in the appeal?
ii) Whether the insurer of TATA 407 is to be exonerated from its liability to pay the compensation in view of violation of condition of policy of insurance i.e. running of vehicle without permit?
iii) What order?
16. The learned advocate for the appellants has vehemently contended that the Tribunal has not considered the income of the deceased properly.

petition averments, he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month from the transport business,
Rs.20,000/- per month from provision store and Rs.2,00,000/- per annum from agriculture.

For the sake of discussion, even if it was considered that the petitioner had not proved that the deceased was earning the above said amount, at least the Tribunal ought to have considered income of the deceased as Rs.8,750/- per month as notional income, as it was normally considered while settling matter in the Lok Adalat for the accident taken place during the year 2016.
The Tribunal has not considered the future prospects of the deceased.
He was aged about 33 years at the time of the accident.

Therefore, as held in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 40% of the said income has to be added towards future prospects.

sentences.text: The submission of the learned advocate for the appellants/claimants is sustainable.
It is true that, there were no legal evidence to accept the income of the deceased as contended in the petition.
However, the Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the deceased on the basis of the schedule of income taken before the Lok Adalat for settling the dispute.

According to the said schedule, if any accident had taken place during the year 2016, notional income of the victim of the accident or the deceased, who died in the accident, is taken as Rs.8,750/- per month.
The same is taken in the present case.

19. In the case of Pranay Seti(supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, in case of a person who dies in an accident and who had no fixed income, his future prospects has to be considered at the rate of 40% of his notional income and to add in his income.

The same has - 16 - C/W MFA Nos.104100/2017, 102695/2017 and 104101/2017.
to be added to the income of the deceased.
Admittedly, the deceased was married and having wife and a daughter.
Therefore, 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
On the basis of the above said calculation, the income of the deceased per month has to be considered as Rs.8,167/-.
The Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier as 16.

Accordingly, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.8,167x12x16=15,68,064 which is rounded of to Rs.15,68,000/-

and the insurer proves the said breach in view of the mandate under Section 149(1) of the Act.

But, no such order can be passed against the insurer, if, on the facts and circumstances of a case, a finding is given by the Court that the third party (injured or deceased) had played any fraud or was in collusion with the insured, individually or collectively, for a wrongful gain to themselves or cause wrongful loss to the insurer.

(iii) The Court can also fasten the absolute liability on the insurer, if there is any breach of condition which is enumerated under Section 149(2) of the Act or any other condition of the policy if the Insurance Company has waived breach of any such condition or had taken the special responsibility to pay by collecting extra premium by covering any type of risk depending upon facts of each case.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Claimants in MVC No.791/2016 have filed MFA No.103245/2017 claiming for enhancement of compensation and insurer of the vehicle (TATA 407) has filed MFA No.104100/2017 against the said judgment contending that he was not liable to pay the compensation since there was violation of permit condition.
Similarly claimants in MVC 792/2016 have filed MFA No.102595/2017 praying for enhancement of compensation and the insurer of the vehicle filed MFA No.104101/2017 contending that it was not liable to pay the compensation since there was violation of permit condition.
As a result of impact, both the rider of motorcycle sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the spot.
Thereafter, the said Kunju Baba sold the vehicle in favour of S.F. Peerjade of Chikodi without transferring the insurance certificate and also without intimation to the insurer.
During pendency of this appeals, the insurer of TATA 407 has filed I.A. under order XLI Rule 27 of CPC along with permit as well as certificate given by concerned RTO.
However, the Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the deceased on the basis of the schedule of income taken before the Lok Adalat for settling the dispute.
According to the said schedule, if any accident had taken place during the year 2016, notional income of the victim of the accident or the deceased, who died in the accident, is taken as Rs.8,750/- per month.
The petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,57,000/-.
The Tribunal has also not granted proper compensation under other heads.
opennyai_summary.issue:
The following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought in the appeal?
ii) Whether the insurer of TATA 407 is to be exonerated from its liability to pay the compensation in view of violation of condition of policy of insurance i.e. running of vehicle without permit?
iii) What order?

Therefore, if there is any violation of the conditions of the policy, then the insurer shall be directed to pay the - 24 - C/W MFA Nos.104100/2017, 102695/2017 and 104101/2017.
compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
The appellant/insurer has produced the said document under I.A.1/2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC.
Strict rules of procedural law or the Evidence Act are not applicable to the Tribunal.
Under these circumstances, the appellant/insurer need to be permitted to produce the additional evidence i.e. the documents produced along with I.A.1/2022.
Since the said documents are obtained from the Public Office i.e, concerned RTO, hence, there is no need for leading formal evidence to prove the document and hence there is no need for remanding the matter to just mark the said documents.
32.
The accident had taken place on - 26 - C/W MFA Nos.104100/2017, 102695/2017 and 104101/2017.
21.02.2016 and hence as on the date of the accident, the said vehicle was not having valid permit to ply on the public road and respondent No.2 i.e. owner of the vehicle had committed breach of terms of the policy and hence he is liable to pay the compensation.
33.
If liability is not fastened on the insurer of the TATA 407 vehicle, the award of the Tribunal or this Court, more or less, would be an un-executable decree and the victims do not get the fruits of the award and they have to be on streets since the earning member of the family had died in the accident.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3(appellant/insurer)of TATA 407 vehicle which was a package policy.
